title: Amaterasu Mirror Garden: Light Field Atlas
subtitle: A fictional atlas of light and reflective landscapes and field notes.

sections.mission: This fictional project explores fictional atlas of light and reflective landscapes. The record links each illustration to a repeatable observation and makes the fictional setting explicit. The activity is an illustrative research sample.
sections.challenge: How can reflected light reveal patterns in an imagined garden? One image alone cannot show the sequence of changes or explain why an observer chose a particular viewpoint. The fictional setting also needs to be clear so readers do not mistake these illustrations for measured locations. Each entry must retain its place in the sequence and identify what changed since the preceding observation. A reader should be able to compare alternate interpretations and trace them back to the original notes.
approach: Map fictional glints and shadows across a painted terrain. Keep the sketches in a stable sequence. Track each change in an annotated fieldbook.
impact: Create an illustrative atlas of changing light. The resulting example helps readers inspect gradual change and understand how evidence is organized.

research.focus: Exploring the imagined themes of amaterasu mirror garden in a research record. The setting and measurements are fictional. Locations remain imaginary.
